title: LoveBud repository schema-change inventory
scope: Read-only inventory of every repository path that can create, alter, drop, repair, seed, or otherwise change (or claim to change) the database schema, plus the read-only provenance tooling that bounds such change. This is the first small slice of #3458 (design-work item 1: inventory every schema-changing path). It does not execute SQL, open a database connection, or mutate any environment.
non_goals: No Production, staging, Neon, Firebase, or Cloudflare access.
No SQL execution and no migration application.
No modification of any existing migration, runtime, API, auth, UI, or CI behavior.
No promotion of any legacy path to canonical status; classification is descriptive, not an adoption decision.
relation_to_existing_inventory: docs/architecture/migration-path-inventory.json remains the authoritative detailed provenance inventory for the migration/repair/runbook/seed/diagnostic paths it already covers (per-file checksums and evidence). This inventory is a broader schema-change surface catalog: it carries those classifications forward by cross-reference and adds the schema-execution surface the migration-path inventory does not enumerate (CI ephemeral execution, DB-engine test harnesses, test-fixture SQL, read-only provenance/catalog tooling, the reserved canonical stream, and verified-negative runtime surfaces).
canonical_status_note: Vocabulary is intentionally identical to docs/architecture/migration-path-inventory.json so the two inventories do not diverge. CANONICAL_CANDIDATE means a path is part of the future canonical read-only/provenance direction; it is NOT a claim that the path is an approved Production migration route. The committed canonical migration stream is inactive (ADOPTION_REQUIRED) with two catalogued migrations; catalog population is distinct from runner activation/adoption.

field_definitions.operations: Schema/data operation classes present or described (CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, DROP, TRUNCATE, CREATE INDEX, DROP INDEX, CREATE POLICY, ALTER POLICY, ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE TRIGGER, DROP TRIGGER, CREATE FUNCTION, DML, READ_ONLY, VALIDATE).
field_definitions.canonical_status: Classification from canonical_status_enum. Descriptive only; not an adoption decision.
field_definitions.destructive: True if the artifact contains destructive DDL (DROP/TRUNCATE/column removal/constraint removal/type narrowing).
field_definitions.production_capable: True if the artifact is technically a route that could change a Production schema when executed by an operator. Read-only validators, ephemeral-CI fixtures/tests, disposable loopback adapters, and pure-JS cores are false.
field_definitions.execution_actor: operator | ci | test_harness | runner | developer | none.
field_definitions.ledger_candidate: Whether the path is a candidate for the future canonical migration ledger: yes | no | pending_owner_decision.
field_definitions.notes: Short evidence and disposition note. Never contains credentials, connection strings, endpoints, database identifiers, row data, or operator identity.

guard.purpose: Static, source-only guard that fails closed when a new schema-changing artifact appears in the repository but is not registered in this inventory. It is an inventory-omission guard, NOT a proof that any PostgreSQL behavior executed correctly.
detection_rules: RULE_SQL: every tracked *.sql file (outside excluded directories) must be registered.

RULE_DDL_SCRIPT: every tracked *.cjs/*.js/*.mjs/*.py file under scripts/, modal_compute/, or functions/ whose content contains a DDL statement pattern (CREATE TABLE/INDEX/POLICY/TRIGGER/SCHEMA, CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION, ALTER TABLE/POLICY, DROP TABLE/INDEX/TRIGGER, TRUNCATE, ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY) must be registered.

RULE_RUNNER_NAME: every tracked non-test *.cjs/*.js/*.mjs/*.py/*.sh/*.ps1 file (outside tests/ and excluded directories) whose basename signals a migration runner or schema repair path (migration|rollback|seed|repair|reconcile|adopt|inspect-schema|verify-db) must be registered.

RULE_DOC_SQL: every tracked *.md file under docs/ops/, docs/architecture/, or docs/product/ whose basename signals an operator/runbook/manual procedure (runbook|migrat|repair|recover|reconcil|rollback|foothold|bulk|seed) AND that embeds a fenced ```sql code block containing a DDL statement pattern must be registered. Precision = runbook-style name AND fenced DDL, which excludes explanatory naming/status/audit docs and prose-only architecture docs (their DDL mentions are not executable procedures).
guard.false_positive_policy: Documentation prose, generated files, vendor files, and the inventory/guard artifacts themselves are explicitly excluded. Test harnesses under tests/ are curated as entries but are not auto-detected by RULE_DDL_SCRIPT/RULE_RUNNER_NAME; *.sql fixtures under tests/db-engine/fixtures/ ARE detected by RULE_SQL and must be registered. For markdown, RULE_DOC_SQL requires BOTH a runbook-style document name AND a fenced ```sql block containing DDL; this avoids false positives from naming-convention examples (e.g. DATA_NAMING_RULE.md), status/audit documents, and prose-only architecture documents that merely discuss DDL.
verified_negative_invariants: modal_compute/**/*.py must contain no literal schema-changing DDL. This is a hard invariant: a violation fails the guard regardless of inventory registration.

functions/**/*.{js,cjs,mjs} must contain no literal schema-changing DDL. This is a hard invariant: a violation fails the guard regardless of inventory registration (registering a path does NOT satisfy it).
guard.limitation: This guard is a static inventory-completeness check plus two verified-negative DDL invariants (modal_compute Python, functions runtime). It does not connect to PostgreSQL, does not run migrations, and does not guarantee runtime schema correctness.

verified_negative_surfaces.notes: Modal Python runtime data-access layer. Verified to contain no literal DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP/TRUNCATE/INDEX/POLICY/TRIGGER/SCHEMA). It issues DML only and is not a schema-change path. Schema authority stays out-of-band and separately approved. Enforced by a hard verified-negative invariant in the guard test: any literal DDL under modal_compute/**/*.py fails the test regardless of inventory registration.

Cloudflare Pages Functions (same-origin /api entry). Verified to contain no inline DDL and no direct DB schema operations; requests proxy to Modal. Not a schema-change path. Enforced by a hard verified-negative invariant in the guard test: any literal DDL under functions/**/*.{js,cjs,mjs} fails the test regardless of inventory registration (registering a path does NOT satisfy it).

Source-tested injected PostgreSQL pinned-session advisory-lock adapter contract (not a real DB client). Implements the orchestrator's acquireAdvisoryLock/checkAdvisoryLock/releaseAdvisoryLock dependency contract: one global per-database lock keyed by a fixed two-int pair, a single pinned session from acquire through release, non-blocking pg_try_advisory_lock, current-session pg_locks verification, explicit pg_advisory_unlock, exactly-once pool release, an opaque frozen handle, and sanitized status-only results. All three public methods are total and fail-closed: safe own-data property inspection never executes accessor getters and never throws, so throwing getters, Proxy traps, revoked Proxies, getPrototypeOf/descriptor-inspection throws, and malformed evidence map to the fixed fail-closed statuses (NOT_ATTEMPTED/UNAVAILABLE for acquire, FAILED/UNAVAILABLE for check, UNKNOWN for release) with no raw error exposure; the factory maps any config.openSession access failure to POSTGRES_LOCK_ADAPTER_OPEN_SESSION_REQUIRED. No pg import, no connection, no actual query execution, no real lock, no Production mutation; all sessions/queries are synthetic injected mocks. Detected by RULE_RUNNER_NAME because the basename contains 'migration'; registered here to satisfy the guard.

Source-tested injected PostgreSQL migration-ledger read/append adapter contract (not a real DB client). Implements the orchestrator's readLedger/appendLedgerRecord dependency contract over a fixed schema_migration_ledger relation and a fixed seven-field order (migration_id, content_checksum, applied_at, runner_version, environment_class, deployed_commit, transaction_outcome). readLedger issues the exact named read query lovebud-migration-ledger-read-v1 (ordered SELECT, no SELECT *, no interpolation, no offset/limit) once, validates QueryResult evidence, and returns a frozen array of frozen seven-field clones preserving row order; an empty ledger is a frozen []. Any failure rejects with the fixed sanitized error POSTGRES_LEDGER_READ_UNAVAILABLE and never returns [] on failure. appendLedgerRecord is total: it snapshots a validated exact-seven-key COMMITTED record before the query, issues the append-only named query lovebud-migration-ledger-append-v1 (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (migration_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING migration_id, content_checksum; no UPDATE/UPSERT-DO-UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/retry/multi-row), and maps exact one matching returned row to APPENDED, rows:[] to FAILED, and any throw/reject/malformed/multi-row/wrong-id-or-checksum/extra-field/Proxy-trap evidence to UNKNOWN; invalid input is FAILED with zero queries. Both methods are fail-closed: safe own-data inspection never executes accessor getters and never throws, so throwing getters, Proxy traps, revoked Proxies, getPrototypeOf/ownKeys/descriptor throws, sparse arrays, custom prototypes, and enumerable symbol extra fields map to the fixed fail-closed outcomes with no raw error/row/handle/session/credential exposure; the factory maps any config.queryLockedSession access failure to POSTGRES_LEDGER_ADAPTER_QUERY_LOCKED_SESSION_REQUIRED. The opaque lockHandle is forwarded unchanged and never inspected/serialized/exposed. No pg import, no connection, no actual query execution, no real ledger read/write, no Production mutation; all queries are synthetic injected mocks. Detected by RULE_RUNNER_NAME because the basename contains 'migration'; registered here to satisfy the guard.
